drhp.business: Hemisphere Properties India Limited (HPIL) was incorporated to receive the surplus land of erstwhile Videsh Sanchar Nigam Limited and holds, protects and seeks to realise value from those land parcels through transparent e-auctions, leasing and planned development. It currently earns recurring income from leasing land and buildings at Pune, and completed the first major monetisation of its land bank with the e-auction of the Bopkhel (Pune) parcel after the close of FY26. The Company reports a single segment and runs with a lean team of five employees supported by specialised consultants.
drhp.end_markets: Delhi (Greater Kailash and Chhatarpur land parcels)|Pune (Dighi/Bopkhel land parcel)|Chennai (Padiyanallur land parcel)|Kolkata (Halisahar land parcel)
drhp.expansion: HPIL has no manufacturing capacity; its expansion narrative is land preparation and monetisation. For the Bopkhel (Pune) parcel, after the change in land use from Public/Semi-Public to Residential and approval of a tentative layout under UDCPR, an RFP was floated on 18 February 2026; the e-auction on 12 May 2026 (after year-end) was won by Hypervault AI Data Center Ltd, shareholder approval was obtained and a Letter of Acceptance issued, with consideration to be received in tranches before the sale deed is executed. For the balance Pune land the Company is evaluating development models spanning residential, commercial, institutional and supporting infrastructure, including an Integrated Township Project model. Renovation and refurbishment works were undertaken on the two buildings the Company owns at Pune, one of which was leased to a Government Department. At Halisahar (Kolkata), ground-level works (internal access, site clearing and preliminary activities) were initiated to facilitate planning through the Transaction Advisor. The Company states it has received in-principle approval for funding in the form of equity and loan towards stamp duty for title transfer and working capital, with the balance expected in tranches or a lump sum per the Ministry of Finance's decision (amount not legible in the text). Security and maintenance of all land assets are handled through CPWD.

litigation.note: Qualitative only: the Directors' Report states physical demarcation of a South Delhi land parcel (designated Public & Semi-Public; parcel name not stated in that paragraph) remains pending due to ongoing litigations; the Chairperson's message states land-related matters are pursued before courts and authorities, with some cases resolved during the year and the remainder still being pursued; MD&A lists Litigation & Encroachment Risk. No amounts read.

risks.note: Pending mutation, registration and other statutory formalities on certain parcels may delay transactions; on one parcel the mutation/patta application was not accepted by the State Revenue Authority because of pending litigation over possession, and at Pune mutation is complete for only about 524 acres with municipal-record applications for the remaining villages still being pursued.

Value realisation depends on land-use, zoning and layout approvals; the Chhatarpur (Delhi) change-of-use application to DDA (PSP to Residential Farm Housing), filed 28 October 2022, remains under consideration pending finalisation of the Master Plan for Delhi 2041.

Certain parcels are exposed to litigation, third-party claims or encroachment; physical demarcation of an upscale South Delhi parcel designated Public & Semi-Public (described as one of the highest per-acre value holdings) remains pending due to ongoing litigations.
The Company itself flags concentration risk from its holdings situated in Pune, mitigated only by opportunities across parcels in other cities.
Economic conditions, interest rates, market sentiment, competing land supply and regulatory restrictions may affect demand and land values.

Delay or non-performance by developers, consultants or strategic partners, and approval or infrastructure constraints, may affect project execution as the Company moves toward development and partnership models.

Availability and cost of funds may constrain operational flexibility and future development; funding for stamp duty and working capital depends on release in tranches or a lump sum per the Ministry of Finance's decision.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:

- Healthy residential demand across metros, with premium/luxury gaining prominence and mid-income remaining important

- Industrial and logistics demand supported by manufacturing, e-commerce, 3PL and PM Gati Shakti / PLI schemes
- Growing institutional participation, including REITs, broadening the investor base for Indian real estate

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Monetise the land bank through transparent, competitive e-auctions; the Bopkhel (Pune) parcel of approximately 88 acres was re-offered as a single consolidated parcel after the 3 October 2025 auction failed, and the fresh RFP of 18 February 2026 succeeded
- For the remaining Pune land, evaluate an Integrated Township Project (ITP) model, subject to statutory approvals, technical feasibility and commercial viability
- Chhatarpur (New Delhi) parcel: studies and assessments under way to decide the most suitable development / value-realisation route
- Halisahar (Kolkata) parcel: ground-level works initiated and options evaluated through Transaction Advisor JLL, with gated residential plots emerging as one potential option
- Complete pending land-related and statutory formalities and approvals with Government and regulatory authorities
- Generate recurring revenue by leasing land and buildings at Pune (rental income from Tata Communications Limited and STT Global Data Centres for access use; one of two Pune buildings leased to a Government Department)
- Evaluate development, leasing and other commercially viable models for the remaining properties
